summary: This paper presents a carefully preregistered, fully archived paired study comparing a syntax-only verifier to a guarded (syntax+policy+reachability+stateful) verifier on 100 seeded NetOps tasks generated by gpt-5-mini. Execution and analysis artifacts are thorough and well-hashed; the confirmatory outcome is unambiguous: both verifiers accepted every shared candidate (100/100), producing a ceiling result that prevents evaluation of the preregistered ≥15pp effect. The work contributes an artifact-rich reproducibility bundle and clear lessons about task-bank design for measuring marginal verifier value, but the manuscript omits a few concise, artifact-resolvable items that reviewers will reasonably expect to see in-text.
critical_issues: Manuscript omits a compact, in-text summary (table) of per-task counts by the preregistered failure-taxonomy leaf classes (syntax, policy-violation, reachability-break, stateful-emulation, ambiguous-intent). The authoritative labels exist in execution/task_manifest.jsonl but are not summarized in the paper.

The paper does not explicitly and prominently state, within Methods, the practical consequence of using the preregistered shared_initial protocol (independent_condition_generation = false): because one identical LLM candidate was scored by both verifiers, the design necessarily reduces the opportunity for discordant accept/reject outcomes and therefore limits the experiment's ability to detect marginal verifier differences. This limitation should be stated clearly and tied to the statistical interpretation (degenerate McNemar/CI).

The manuscript does not include the exact generation prompt(s) (or a representative exemplar) used to produce the shared_initial candidate in the confirmatory runs. Provider-call artifacts exist (execution/provider_calls/*.json) and are hashed, so an explicit in-manuscript pointer plus a short quoted exemplar prompt should be added for transparency and reproducibility.
required_revisions: Add a one-paragraph in Methods and a compact table (1–2 lines or small table) showing counts/proportions of the 100 confirmatory tasks per preregistered taxonomy leaf (syntax, policy-violation, reachability-break, stateful-emulation, ambiguous-intent). Populate this table directly from execution/task_manifest.jsonl (use its archived SHA and cite the file path).

Explicitly state in Methods (and restate in Discussion) that the preregistered shared_initial generation (independent_condition_generation = false) produced one identical candidate per task that both verifiers scored, explain how that design feature deterministically reduces chances for discordant pairs, and add a short sentence interpreting why the McNemar test and the bootstrap CI are uninformative under complete saturation (n10=n01=0). Cite the deterministic artifact (execution/provider_calls/* and execution/responses/* SHA entries) supporting the identical-response observation.

Insert the exact text of the shared_initial generation prompt (or a single representative exemplar prompt) used in the confirmatory generation into the Methods or Disclosure Statement (strictly within the five-page limit). If space is constrained, include a single short quoted exemplar prompt and give the authoritative provider_calls file path(s) and SHA‑256s (already archived) for full prompt provenance.
optional_revisions: Consider adding a single-row summary in Results that lists the number of tasks whose 'difficulty.level' is 'semantic' or 'ambiguous-intent' (if any), to emphasize where future banks should focus.
Shorten or relocate one representative figure/caption to accommodate the small table and prompt excerpt while keeping the PDF ≤5 pages.

In Discussion, more explicitly recommend (and reference the archived task_manifest fields) precise task‑bank construction heuristics (e.g., % ambiguous-intent targets, adversarial phrasing templates, and per-task multiple-generation draws) to guide follow-up studies.
